title: A pilot study on the effect of body-focused cognitive bias modification training on the reduction of negative body-related attitudes amongst female patients with eating disorders and depression.
summary:
Many adolescents experience a negative perception of their own bodies, which is often linked to low self-esteem and depressive symptoms. Research suggests that body perception and mood are closely interconnected and may influence each other over time.

The aim of this study is to examine whether a training designed to modify body perception can help reduce depressive symptoms and improve body image.

The study includes female adolescents who are receiving inpatient treatment for depression. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group receives a computer-based training in addition to their usual treatment, in which they repeatedly evaluate images of bodies. The other group receives usual treatment only. Assessments are conducted before the training, immediately after the intervention, and at a follow-up. These include questionnaires on mood, body image, and self-esteem, as well as tasks measuring body perception.

interventions.name: Patients of the Intervention group (CBM + TAU) receive Treatment as Usual (TAU) plus six sessions of 2-AFC Cognitive Bias Modification (CBM) training within 2 to 3 weeks. Each session includes the BISS and the 2-AFC task (baseline, training with corrective feedback targeting a +2 BMI shift, and post
Patients of the Control group (TAU) receive TAU without CBM.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Inpatient treatment at the LWL University Hospital Hamm
- Primary diagnosis: Moderate depressive episode (ICD-10: F32.1)
- Sufficient German language skills for questionnaire completion
- Written consent from legal guardians
Exclusion criteria:
Primary, currently active eating disorder (e.g., anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa)
- Eating disorder as comorbid diagnosis
- Severe psychiatric comorbidities (e.g., psychosis, acute suicidality)
- Neurological or organic disorders affecting perception or cognition
- Participation in other psychological studies during the study period
